//Kestrel: Named rather than inherited: a framework default you rely on is still a decision, and an unnamed
one cannot be changed by an operator or reviewed by anyone. Both values here happen to match
Kestrel's own defaults today — that is the point, they are now written down and configurable.
KeepAliveTimeout bounds an IDLE connection between requests; it does not touch an open SSE stream,
which is why the MCP transport is unaffected. RequestHeadersTimeout is the slowloris bound: a
client that opens a socket and never finishes its headers costs a connection for exactly this long.
//Mcp: RequestTimeout applies to /api/mcp/* ONLY — never as a global default, because MapMcp() serves a
Server-Sent Events stream meant to stay open. A tool call is bounded instead by the catalog's
ToolCatalogOptions.CallTimeout (2 minutes), at the one dispatch chokepoint. These two are chosen
against each other: the management API answers in milliseconds, so 30s is already generous, and
raising it past the catalog's ceiling would only mean waiting on a call the server has given up on.
//Mcp:Logs: RetentionDays prunes log DAY FOLDERS older than the window, once, at startup. Zero or negative keeps
everything — a deliberate off switch, because a misread config that silently deleted a month of logs
would be the worst possible failure of a retention feature.
It does NOT touch the telemetry spool. That is drained by a consumer which owns its own retention
(bench telemetry prune, in dew_flow_benchmark); deleting a spool file here would destroy records
nobody has ingested, and this process cannot know which those are.
